correctness.rationale: Translate coordinates so the common rotation center is the origin. The planar convex anisotropic Cheeger theorem gives C=(Omega minus rho W) plus rho W and uniqueness. Any orthogonal Q preserving both Omega and W commutes exactly with Minkowski erosion and addition, hence QC=C. Cyclic rotation groups of orders k and k_tilde intersect in the subgroup of order gcd(k,k_tilde), and k divides k_tilde makes the domain generator a W symmetry. For contact, a boundary point z of the erosion has z+rho W inside Omega; if this translate had positive clearance from the boundary then z would be interior to the erosion, a contradiction. A resulting point of C on boundary Omega lies on boundary C, and the k-fold orbit supplies a contact in every cyclic edge.
risks: The divisibility condition is sufficient, not necessary; accidental extra symmetry is possible.
Nonconvex domains are outside the uniqueness/structure hypotheses.
